facts.statement: Bountyphaps obsoleta was described in 2008 based on subfossil remains discovered on Henderson Island in the Pitcairn Group of southeastern Polynesia.
facts.quote: It was described in 2008 from subfossil remains found on Henderson Island in the Pitcairn Group of southeastern Polynesia.

facts.statement: An indeterminate species, possibly the same as Bountyphaps obsoleta, has also been found in the Gambier archipelago.
facts.quote: Additionally, an indeterminate species, possibly the same as B. obsoleta, has been found in the Gambier archipelago.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the ship HMS Bounty, which brought Europeans to the islands, and the food value the bird provided.
facts.quote: The genus was named for both the ship HMS Bounty with which, following the famous mutiny, Europeans first discovered the Pitcairn Islands, and for the former bounty the bird provided as food

facts.statement: The specific epithet obsoleta derives from the Latin adjective meaning "extinct" or "forgotten about".
facts.quote: The specific epithet comes from the Latin adjective for "extinct" or "forgotten about".

facts.statement: The species was described from 18 bones found at four archaeological sites on Henderson Island, primarily from early Polynesian middens.
facts.quote: It was described from 18 bones from four archaeological sites on Henderson Island, mainly from early Polynesian middens.

facts.statement: While its affinities are uncertain, comparisons suggest Bountyphaps is most closely related to living species like the Nicobar pigeon or tooth-billed pigeon, and by extension, the dodo.
facts.quote: The affinities of the new genus are uncertain, but comparisons with other taxa suggest that, among living species, it is most closely related to the Nicobar pigeon or the tooth-billed pigeon — and, by extension, the dodo.

facts.statement: Bountyphaps became extinct following human colonization of Henderson Island, an event that occurred by 1050 CE.
facts.quote: The pigeon became extinct following human colonisation of Henderson, an event that had occurred by 1050 CE.

facts.statement: The species lived during the Holocene, from 0.0117 million years ago to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Holocene to Holocene (0.0117 to 0 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The species was a large pigeon, comparable in size to large species of Columba or Ducula, and larger than the other three species of pigeon it coexisted with on the island.
